source.title: STU-Net: Scalable and Transferable Medical Image Segmentation Models Empowered by Large-Scale Supervised Pre-training
source.authors: Zi-Yan Huang; Hao Wang; Zhong-Ying Deng; Jin Ye; Yan-Zhou Su; Hui Sun; Jun-Jun He; Yun Gu; Li-Xu Gu; Shao-Ting Zhang; Y. Qiao

record.file_problem: The text is largely readable and appears to be the full paper, but some extracted figure and table text has encoding artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates how medical image segmentation performance varies with model scale on direct-inference and fine-tuning downstream tasks. This is an extension to medical image segmentation, not a test of language-model cross-entropy scaling laws.
record.gate_note: Rows are limited to the downstream-task scaling results bearing on V6. The paper cites Kaplan et al. as background but does not test language-model loss power laws, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation. Its upstream scaling and architecture-ablation results do not measure downstream-task performance and are not included.
record.test_reason: The study trains 3D CNN medical segmentation models (STU-Net, 14M–1.4B parameters). It cites Kaplan et al. only as background. It never fits a power law, never measures held-out loss, and studies no language model. Its downstream Dice-vs-size results compare 3 model sizes and fit no predictive law. So they do not bear on V6, which concerns language-model downstream predictability (other systems fall under V5). They also do not bear on V5, which requires the power-law form. The size-scaling findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Roughly right. The authors conclude that scaling STU-Net size improves segmentation on TotalSegmentator and transfer to downstream tasks, and that pre-training plus fine-tuning adds further gains. They also find compound depth+width scaling best. They note that from scratch the huge model is slightly worse than the large one, which they attribute to limited data.
record.recipe_differences: Three-dimensional medical image segmentation models are evaluated using Dice scores on medical datasets; the study does not measure language-model next-token cross-entropy or fit scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by downstream dataset and by whether models are evaluated by direct inference, trained from scratch, or fine-tuned from TotalSegmentator pre-training.

fits_no_version.finding: In STU-Net segmentation CNNs, TotalSegmentator validation Dice rises with size: S 83.74, B 87.12, L 88.71, H 90.06 (Table 3). Compound depth+width scaling beats depth-only or width-only scaling (Table 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-LM vision segmentation models improve monotonically with parameter count, but no power-law form is shown.

fits_no_version.finding: Direct-inference mean Dice over 14 datasets rises B 80.71, L 82.83, H 84.02, with non-monotonic series on several datasets. Fine-tuned means rise 79.23/80.19/80.69, but scratch-trained H (77.64) falls below L (77.80).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream gains from scale in medical segmentation are monotonic on average after pre-training, but not per dataset or when trained from scratch on small data.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 4: Dice improves with the fraction of training cases for all sizes and is not saturated; larger models are more data-efficient.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data scaling in segmentation improves performance without a fitted law.

record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for these results. Its downstream scale comparisons use mean DSC rather than a fitted predictive law, and some dataset-specific or scratch-trained results do not increase monotonically with size.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached. Omitted Table 4 nnU-Net per-dataset comparator rows; the Table 4 aggregate nnU-Net result is retained. Omitted Table 5 metrics other than the aggregate mean and AutoPET-CT values, including FLARE22, AMOS, AMOS-CT, AMOS-MR, AutoPET, and AutoPET-PET. Other upstream scaling and architecture results in Tables 3, 6, and 7 do not measure downstream-task performance for V6.

untested.parts: No language-model loss, no power-law fit in parameters, data or compute.
No extrapolation from fitted small runs.
Depth vs width ablation (Table 7) is on a segmentation CNN, not LM loss.
Other modality (3D medical segmentation), but Dice only at 4 sizes and no power-law form is fitted or tested.
No language-model downstream tasks; no predictive relation to scale or pretraining loss is fitted.
No exponents or fitting choices compared.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'tests' call is overturned. V5 exists for non-text settings, which implies V6 concerns language models. Even if one read the study under V5, it shows only monotonic gains at 3–4 sizes with no power-law fit, so it cannot speak to the claimed form. No uncertainty is reported. Scratch-trained rows carry a misleading 'fine-tuning results table' condition.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model held-out cross-entropy or power-law relationship in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No power-law fits or predictions from small language-model runs are evaluated.
No fixed-compute language-model allocation between parameters and tokens is studied.
No fixed-parameter comparison of language-model loss across architectures is made.
The paper studies medical images but does not test whether a power-law form holds in another modality or training regime.
The study evaluates medical segmentation DSC, not language-model downstream tasks or relationships between downstream performance and pretraining loss; it reports no predictive power-law fit.
No language-model scaling-law exponents, fit choices, or compute-optimal allocations are compared.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Aggregate direct inference across 14 downstream datasets and aggregate fine-tuned results
reader_labels.reason: The direct-inference mean rises from STU-Net-B to STU-Net-H, and the fine-tuned aggregate mean rises from STU-Net-B-ft to STU-Net-H-ft (dmb, dml, dmh, tmean_bft, tmean_lft, tmean_hft).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Individual direct-inference datasets, scratch-trained downstream models, and AutoPET-CT
reader_labels.reason: Several direct-inference dataset series are non-monotonic, scratch-trained aggregate performance falls from STU-Net-L to STU-Net-H, and AutoPET-CT scratch results are non-monotonic; fine-tuned AutoPET-CT scores, in contrast, increase with scale (d3b–d3h, d5b–d5h, d9b–d9h, d13b–d13h, tmean_b–tmean_h, apct_b–apct_h, apct_bft–apct_hft).
